lowBlow.flavor:
Strike below the belt.

Forbidden by the Court's code of arms, which hangs upon the Citadel gate in frost-bitten gilt. The children of the docks read it aloud to one another in jest.

Its final clause, on the treatment of the unmarked, has been chipped from the stone.

lowGuardRiposte.flavor:
The worn stones teach the lower answer.

Recruits practiced on the Bastion's worn courtyard until their boots found the same stones without looking. Veterans watched the shoulders rather than the weapon. After the Burning, the surviving lessons were passed from one tired pair of hands to another.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

lowGuardRiposte.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Counter Melee attacks for 3 Poise; +2 Poise while Prone.

lucidRecovery.flavor:
The apprentice rises from the reflected chair.

The apprentices worked beside darkened lenses until they could distinguish a reflection from its source. One kept a second chair for a companion nobody else remembered. The chair was found warm after the Observatory had stood empty for years.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

lucidRecovery.textTemplate: Break {removeStatus} Sleep. If asleep when played, gain {gainBarrier} Barrier.

lucidity.flavor:
Clarity for the work.

Practised on the one clear night in forty the reach allowed. The Astronomer worked such nights without sleep, and bade his apprentices do the same.

They believed he saw more than the charts show, and wrote it elsewhere.
lucidity.name: Lucidity

martyrBlood.flavor:
Offering of the Saint's own blood.

Made at the altar when the censer ran low, for a Saint's blood was held to burn hotter than any incense. When the censers were cleaned in the years of the Spire, dried blood lay layered beneath the ash.

We spend ourselves at the altar, and the censer swings faster.
martyrBlood.name: Martyr's Blood
martyrBlood.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Gain {gainEnergy} Stamina. Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

masterOfStrategy.flavor:
Maps scratched upon cairn stones.

Left by climbers who came back down, or meant to. The hamlet councils copy the true ones and burn the rest, and each winter argue which were which.

The oldest shows a fourth road leading off the ring toward the coast. It has not been burned.
masterOfStrategy.name: Master of Strategy

meteorSwarm.flavor:
Many falls, called as one.

Chart 43 records two falls in a single night. Miners were sent to both sites and found no crater at either. The Astronomer entered both regardless, for his lens could not err.

A third mark on chart 43, in another ink, is nowhere explained.
meteorSwarm.name: Meteor Swarm
meteorSwarm.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Starstone: {damage.2} again.

meteorite.flavor:
Heavy fall, called upon one enemy.

The largest fragment the Starwatch recovered weighed more than its size allowed. The miners who carried it said it weighed more atop the stair than at its foot.

The Astronomer had it weighed at both ends, and recorded the results in cipher.
meteorite.name: Meteorite

mindFracture.flavor:
A crack drawn through the self.

The Starwatch's examiners tested apprentices by asking which memory they would give up. The ones who answered quickly were sent to the lower lenses. The ones who hesitated were kept.

Neither group was told what the examiners took.
mindFracture.name: Mind Fracture
mindFracture.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Apply {confused} Confused.

mindSpike.flavor:
A needle of thought, set where the doubt already lives.

The Starwatch drilled its apprentices to name a stranger's fear before the stranger did. The best of them could do it across a courtyard, and the worst of them could not stop.

The lens room was always quiet after the drill.
mindSpike.name: Mind Spike
mindSpike.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Psychic damage leaves the target Confused.

misdirect.flavor:
Art of leading the watch astray.

Perfected on the night of the Courtly Decree, when the brand-men came down to the river to mark the last of the unmarked by dawn, and the ice-cutters paid the bridge watch to lead them in circles.

The Decree said dawn. On that side of the river, dawn came late.
misdirect.name: Misdirect
misdirect.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies. Become Prepared.

moonlitShieldCard.flavor:
Frost raised by moonlight upon starstone.

It rises along the rails of Starwatch Terrace on clear nights, where the apprentices once judged the cold by it. From the Tidebound Chapel across the water, the salt-priests have watched it form the shape of a word.

They have not written it down.
moonlitShieldCard.name: Moonlit Shield
moonlitShieldCard.textTemplate: Whenever you gain Starstone Charge, gain 3 Block.

moonrendCut.flavor:
Crescent stroke of the Observatory's night-porters.

The porters walked the Basalt Stair with lanterns and curved blades, and claimed the moon's passage over the caldera showed them where to cut. The Starwatch called it folklore, and employed them regardless.

Their blades are found in the lower galleries, in hands no longer quite their own.
moonrendCut.name: Moonrend Cut

nockAndWait.flavor:
The string drawn, the breath held.

A dock archer waits for the tide bell, when every head on the quay turns at once. The bell has rung at the wrong hours since the Burning.

The archers have learned to wait for the heads instead.
nockAndWait.name: Nock and Wait
nockAndWait.textTemplate: Prepare Ranged Counter. Draw {draw} cards. Become Prepared.

opportunistCard.flavor:
First law of the frozen docks.

When the knight stumbles, the purse swings. The stitched knights stumble often in their sewn armour, and the docks have prospered by it.

Many of those knights are the fathers and brothers of the docks. This is not spoken of.
opportunistCard.name: Opportunist
opportunistCard.textTemplate: Whenever an enemy Staggers, become Prepared and draw a card.

painOffering.flavor:
Small pain, offered in advance.

Taught to crown-born children as good citizenship; the children called it paying early. The habit outlived the Chapel among the Forsaken hamlets, learned from refugees after the Burning.

They keep it without knowing whom they pay.
painOffering.name: Pain Offering

penance.flavor:
Kneeling upon the cold stone of the nave.

Prescribed for small failings of devotion, until the knees bled. The nave was repaved twice in the years of the Mark Trade, with stone from the caldera, and no reason given.

We kneel on the cold stone and are forgiven.

phoenixChart.flavor:
A chart that redraws itself from its ash.

One page of the burned catalogue did not stay burned. Each dawn it lay whole in the courtyard, its stars a little moved. The apprentices burned it thrice more.

It returned each time, and each time a little warmer to the touch.
phoenixChart.name: Phoenix Chart

pilfer.flavor:
Lift worked in the crowds upon the bridges.

The Court counted wrists and kept careful rolls, but never counted purses. Old Keel, the Tollmouth fence, taught that to rob a courtier sewn to his post was salvage, not theft.

He claimed to have been a courtier once. His wrist bears the brand.

pinningShot.flavor:
An arrow through the hem, not the heart.

Dock archers learned it on the gulls first, then on the Court's bailiffs, whose long coats caught on every piling. A pinned bailiff is a patient one.

The docks still tell which bailiff wore the longest coat, and laugh.
pinningShot.name: Pinning Shot

plagueBearer.flavor:
Office of the censer-bearer.

The Saints taught that the censer's smoke opened doors to the fire's blessing. When the Chapel set the office down, the Feral Ember took it up, and bears the censers lit through the weald.

The doors open for them more readily than ever they did for the Saints.

pocketSand.flavor:
Kiln ash, carried in a coat lining.

From the south-bank lime kilns, where the dock poor laboured for the Court's builders. The Court paid in lime and taxed in coin; the ash was the one thing given freely.

The kilns went cold with the Court Flame. The ash has not run out.

Hands warmed before the work.

Cold hands drop knives. Dock children learn to warm their hands before they learn to steal, and never at a fire another has lit. A borrowed fire is a debt, and the docks collect.

Offer warmth to the hand that remains.

A pilgrim gathered the ashes of a roadside hearth into a little cloth pouch. They carried no heat, but touching the pouch reminded him to tend the living before honoring the dead. Heralds keep the gesture, giving a small kindness room beside the heavier rites.

The living still have a road ahead.

Blank rag upon a pole.

Planted where climbers who meet upon the road may find one another. The Forsaken never had banners, for a banner bears a name. The corrupted come to them too.

A rag on a pole. Find it. Stand by it.

rallyingStandard.flavor:
Banner of the Bastion muster.

Raised when the bell rang the line into place. The drill ends thus: raise the standard, sound the bell, log that the line held.

The final muster is logged as held, at dawn. The Bastion has seen no dawn since the Burning.

readTheAsh.flavor:
Divination by what the fire left behind.

A practice the Astronomer forbade as superstition, and the apprentices kept in secret beneath the terrace stair. They burned a copy of each night's chart and read the ash against it.

The two agreed more often than the Astronomer would have liked.

The ink is fresh. The hand shakes.

restfulDream.flavor:
A darkened lens shelters the weary eye.

The apprentices worked beside darkened lenses until they could distinguish a reflection from its source. One kept a second chair for a companion nobody else remembered. The chair was found warm after the Observatory had stood empty for years.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

ricochet.flavor:
Blade skipped across the ice.

A children's game on the frozen river, played with pebbles by the young and knives by the old. The ice keeps no witnesses, they say.

It is said the Marrow Organist, beneath it, hears every throw.
ricochet.name: Ricochet

rimeNeedle.flavor:
A thin shard opens the winter.

The Starwatch kept bowls of water beside the lenses through winter. Apprentices learned to read the skin of ice before it cracked. Their notes survived the Burning, folded inside cloth that still stiffens when a stranger touches it.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

rimeNeedle.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. May add {frost} frost buildup; upcasting improves its chance.

rimeThrust.flavor:
Frost spear of the Pale Marches.

Its point was reforged from the broken blade of a Court knight, and marches steel keeps its frost long after leaving the cold. The ice-fishers who made it say the knight gave the blade freely, before the Decree, for a winter's fish.

The ice-fishers keep no records.
rimeThrust.name: Rime Thrust

riposte.flavor:
Return off the guard, as the Citadel fencing-masters taught it.

The Court held it too fine for field-born hands. Its manual shows a bout upon the bridges in the first year of the Mark Trade, a Knight against an unnamed Warden, and declares the Knight victorious.

In the illustration, the Knight lies upon his back.

riteOfCinders.flavor:
The embers stirred, and the mind with them.

The apprentices performed it before long watches, breathing the smoke of burned charts until the stars came clearer. The Astronomer called it poisoning. He also asked what they saw.

They saw a great deal. Little of it was in the sky.

rockfall.flavor:
The ceiling remembers it was a hill.

The Chapel's masons propped their vaults with lime and trust. Where the trust ran out, the hill came back down in a single afternoon, and the masons wrote it up as maintenance.

The ledger shows no survivors in the maintenance column either.

rockfall.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Earth damage leaves each target Slowed.

rogueShiv.flavor:
Sliver of iron from the rail of the Fourth Bridge.

The ironwork froze brittle the night the Court Flame died. Dock children say the railings were cast from the Court's melted oath-tokens, and so are worth more than any blade in the right hands.

Whose hands are right, the children will not tell.
rogueShiv.name: Shiv

rondelParry.flavor:
Parry upon the guard of a rondel dagger.

Favoured by the Bastion's older sellswords, who kept the short blade long after the Wardens ceased to issue it. The rondels came from the Northern Holds as tribute, and were worth more than a season's wage.

They bear a crest no herald of the ring recorded.

rotMote.flavor:
A bitter seed forgets the season.

Gardeners beneath the Chapel sifted bitter ash through exhausted soil. A root could be fed or strangled by the same handful, depending on the season. Their last ledger names each bed twice, once for its bloom and once for its silence.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

ruinousBlow.flavor:
Whole-body blow of the Wardens.

Reserved for a gate where all else has failed, and called a Warden's last argument. What becomes of the Warden who makes it, the drill does not say.

The pages that follow are stained through.
ruinousBlow.name: Ruinous Blow

sacredHarvest.flavor:
Harvest rite of the Chapel.

A gilded sickle, blessed and carried through the fields of the crown-born. The Chapel found the harvest beautiful, and built a chapel to it. The rubric lists what the sickle is to cut, in the fields and after.

The second half of the list is written in the old script.
sacredHarvest.name: Sacred Harvest

sanctuaryCleanse.flavor:
The little lamp is tended before the wound.

Pilgrims carried little lamps through the Chapel's long passages, tending each flame before their own food. The rite outlived the voices that taught it. An empty hand held over a stranger's wound still remembers the warmth of that watch.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

sanguinePactCard.flavor:
Soldier's bargain of the Bastion's lesser shrine.

Blood spilled from an enemy is sworn to the one who spilled it. The Wardens thought it a harmless field-born custom, like the harvest tithe. The Chapel called it a mockery of the Writing, and fined the shrine.

The fine was paid. The shrine was in use the night of the Burning.

sanguinePactCard.textTemplate: Whenever Bleed bursts on an enemy, gain 2 Strength.

sap.flavor:
Sand-weighted cosh of the docks.

Meant to fell without killing. It does not work upon the Marionettes, who dance on with slack strings. One thief used it upon a girl at the foot of the Stitched Throne, a dancer no older than a dock child.

He returned asking whether anyone knew the tune she hummed.

scholarsInsight.flavor:
Discipline of the double copy.

Apprentices copied each chart twice, for the second copy is the true one. The two copies of chart 9 differ in a single figure: the distance from the three hearths to a point upon the coast.

Both copies left the Observatory with the apprentice who took the charts.

We walk the nave with the scourge, and the pews answer.

Rite of recovery, named for the weald's second flowering.

The orchards bloomed a second time in years when the Field Flame burned strong, and the Chapel claimed both the blossom and the healing as its work. Neither has come since the Burning.

The last novice performs the rite regardless, and says it works.

septicBlade.flavor:
Edge left unwashed on purpose.

The Court's surgeons scrubbed their blades between patients and were called fussy for it. The docks keep theirs in a jar of the second shelf's dregs and call that discipline.

A wound that has already been poisoned once takes the edge twice as hard.

serratedBlade.flavor:
Saw-backed blade from the forges beneath the Bastion ridge.

Weald smiths filed its teeth for clearing briar, and the Wardens took it up when the Blight came out of the woods. The smiths were never paid for the change of use.

How the briar learned to bleed, the smiths will not speak of.

serratedShiv.flavor:
Shiv sawn from a Marionette's spine-rod.

The Court's surgeons set steel rods in the spines of their dancers, to keep them upright through the dance. Dock thieves call the taking of one a mercy.

The surgeons who fitted them took their reasons beneath the ice.

setTheShield.flavor:
The rim planted, the shoulder behind it.

Old Vanguard drill: the shield is set before the enemy is seen, and the man behind it waits. The drill was called cowardice by the Court's duellists, until the night the Court's gate fell.

The duellists did not drill again.
setTheShield.name: Set the Shield

setupRogue.flavor:
Preparation of a dock job.

A window left open on the Lantern Bridge, a lamp turned low, a guard paid to cough. The method is credited to a thief called the Wick, who planned the first robbery of the Regent's hall in the years of the Mark Trade.

It is said the Court itself paid her to rob it.

shadowstep.flavor:
Step through a pier's shadow.

The shadows beneath the bridges are let by the season, and rent is owed to whoever held the pier before. Tenancies pass down like a trade.

The oldest belongs to one not seen since the Decree. The rent is always paid.

sharedFlame.flavor:
Warmth passed between two climbers.

Hands over one coal, breath beneath one coat, with no hearth and no ledger. The Chapel would have named it theft. It is the only warmth upon the ring owed to no one.

Warmth passed between two outlives the fire.

shatterOpportunity.flavor:
A cracked bowl leaves the water free.

The Starwatch kept bowls of water beside the lenses through winter. Apprentices learned to read the skin of ice before it cracked. Their notes survived the Burning, folded inside cloth that still stiffens when a stranger touches it.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.

shieldBash.flavor:
Rim-strike of the Wardens' shield line.

Drilled in the years of the Spring Wars, when envoys of the Northern Holds came to the Bastion gate to haggle the price of a spring. The Wardens struck with the rim, for the face bore the gilded crest.

Twice the Holds were struck. Twice they paid.

Tower shield from the Bastion's walls.

Heavy as a door, nearly as tall. The Wardens set such shields in the embrasures to fight from, never to carry. Climbers carry them regardless, for a moving wall is better than a still one.

The weight bows the bearer forward, as the Wardens once bowed before the Bastion.

shieldCrash.flavor:
The whole weight of the wall, thrown forward.

A Vanguard shieldman who has held long enough may drive his shield into the line before him. The chronicles of the siege praise it; the surgeons who reset the shieldmen's shoulders afterward do not.

Both kept their records honestly.

shieldGuardian.flavor:
Kite shield of the Court's knights, its strap cut short.

Such shields lie easily found upon the marches road, where the knights who bore them were stitched to their posts and left standing. Climbers take the shields and leave the knights.

The knights have not objected.

shieldwall.flavor:
Formation of the Bastion's shield line.

Rim locked to rim across the Fell Courtyard. The Wardens credited it with holding the gate through three hungry winters of the Spring Wars, when Hold petitioners camped below the walls.

The field-book enters the price of spring in the same column as the petitioners turned away.

shootingShard.flavor:
Small fall, too faint for the charts.

The Starwatch left such falls unrecorded, a star too faint to mark the lens being unworthy of ink. The reach miners kept their own tally, scratched upon the walls of the lower galleries.

Their count runs far higher.

slimed.flavor:
Grey muck from the drowned hamlet.

It clings, and will not wash out in cold water. The hamlet flooded before the Burning, in a flood the Wardens called natural.

It is warmer than anything in the weald has a right to be.

smokeBomb.flavor:
Pig's bladder of kiln ash.

Split upon the stones, it raises a fog the bridge watch reports as a haunting. The ash is from the south-bank kilns, which in the Court's last years were fired with something other than lime.

The reports are not wholly wrong.

The docks buy more of them each winter.

smokeVeil.flavor:
River fog, thickened with ash.

The fog rose off the water the night the Court Flame died, and has not lifted. The Court's lamplighters, paid to burn it away, were the first to be lost in it.

Their guild-book ends with a list of lamps to be relit. None are marked done.

No bearer since has drawn the nails.

Who showed the Astronomer where to draw, the charts do not tell.

starSlicer.flavor:
Starstone, split along its grain.

The stone parts cleanly along lines the lens-grinders could see and the miners could not. The grinders held that it had been worked before it fell. The Astronomer called this sentimental.

He kept a split fragment upon his desk, its grain turned to the window.

starSpark.flavor:
Spark struck from a starstone flint.

The chart room kept such a flint for its lamps, for the Astronomer would not suffer the Chapel's flame in that room. Its sparks died before they landed.

Maud Vell said the stone was being careful.

starbladePhalanx.flavor:
Blades ground from a single stone.

The apprentices found that blades from one stone answered one another in sequence, the second truer than the first. The Chapel's censor struck "answered" from the record and wrote "rang".

The apprentices kept the first word.

starcaller.flavor:
Many falls, called in rhythm.

The apprentices chanted the star tables while practising it in the lens gallery, and on the night it was first attempted, eleven falls were recorded. The Astronomer entered chant and falls upon the same line.

He drew no connection between them. He drew none between anything.

starfallBeam.flavor:
Column of falling light.

Modelled upon a fall the Astronomer charted in advance. He foresaw where it would strike upon the caldera rim, and sent no warning to the mine camps there, for they were unmarked, and absent from the Court's maps.

His margin gives the fall's weight to the grain. Of the camps, nothing.

starfallBeam.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

stargazerCard.flavor:
The long watch at the eyepiece.

The Astronomer kept it a hundred years by his own count, recording the coal's dimming and never its meaning. The Chapel admired his restraint.

His apprentices believed he watched something he had already resolved not to describe.
stargazerCard.name: Stargazer
stargazerCard.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain Starstone Charge.

starlance.flavor:
Light forced through a starstone lens.

Discovered when the great lens scorched a line across the chart-room table. The Astronomer had the table kept as it was, and recorded that the line ran true to the south-west.

The line has lengthened since.
starlance.name: Starlance

starstoneArc.flavor:
Arc of force, used to measure the stone's reach.

Measured three times, the stone was found to have moved between readings. The Starwatch recorded an error of the apparatus, and replaced it.

The same error is recorded each month, until the eclipse.

starstoneKris.flavor:
Wavy dagger of starstone.

Carried by apprentices for rough work in the lower galleries. Its first owner wrapped it in cloth and found the cloth frosted by morning. The kris keeps its cold whether carried or not.

It was coldest, the apprentice noted, in the Astronomer's presence.
starstoneKris.name: Starstone Kris
starstoneKris.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: draw {draw} card and deal {damage.2} again.

starstonePebble.flavor:
Chip of catalogued starstone.

Such stones were weighed and numbered by the Observatory's apprentices in their first winter. The Astronomer held them inert once cooled, and wrote as much throughout his catalogue.

Yet frost formed upon their labels by night. Never upon the stones.
starstonePebble.name: Starstone Pebble

starstoneWard.flavor:
Slab of starstone, raised as a shield.

After the fashion of the Observatory's doors, cut by builders whose name the Chapel did not keep. Starstone stays cold where all else warms.

The apprentices believed those doors were not made to open from within.
starstoneWard.name: Starstone Ward

staticNeedle.flavor:
The smallest spark still seeks iron.

Storms found the Observatory's iron stairs long before any scholar could name their path. Apprentices marked the scorched rails, then wrapped their hands in dry cloth. The surviving diagrams begin with a warning to watch where the current returns.

The lesson outlived the hands that first carried it.
staticNeedle.name: Static Needle
staticNeedle.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. May add {paralysis} paralysis buildup; upcasting improves its chance.

stigmataCard.flavor:
Marks of the Saints.

Worn openly upon hands and brow, and held by the Chapel to be a favour of the fire. Novices learned they appeared more reliably upon Saints with a knife at hand.

Novice Wen wrote so plainly, then begged forgiveness for it, twice.
stigmataCard.name: Stigmata
stigmataCard.textTemplate: Whenever you lose HP, heal 2 HP.

stitchCrab.seamShears.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Apply {bleed} Bleed to the enemy.

stitchedArms.flavor:
Swordwork of the Court's stitched knights.

After the Court Flame died, the surgeons sewed the knights to their swords, that no oath might be set down. The Citadel's record names it an honour: a knight's word made flesh.

The record was written by the surgeons.

stomp.flavor:
Heel-strike of the Fell Courtyard.

The Wardens named it unworthy and used it all the same, for in the courtyard the fallen seldom stayed down. Sellswords held that the Wardens objected only to being seen at it.

Many an old Bastion helm bears the dent of a heel.

stoneSling.flavor:
A pebble from the broken stair, thrown with the whole wrist.

The Basalt Stair porters kept a sling in each apron to scatter the crows from the grain. The crows learned to leave. The Stair's other visitors were slower learners.

The porters have not been paid in years and still keep their slings oiled.
stoneSling.name: Stone Sling
stoneSling.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Earth damage leaves the target Slowed.

stoneskin.flavor:
The body takes the temper of the quarry.

Bastion masons rubbed grit into their forearms until the grit stayed. They said a wall that forgets to be a wall is only a heap, and a mason who forgets is the same.

The hardest of them could not be moved, and some of them could not move.
stoneskin.name: Stoneskin
stoneskin.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block and {stoneskin} Stoneskin: your Block is not removed at the start of your next turn.

strike.flavor:
First cut of the hamlets.

Made with whatever edge the hamlet owns. Marl's Hollow sends one climber each winter, chosen at the well, and the chosen spends the last evening at the whetting post learning this and nothing more.

The marked learned a thousand cuts. It did them no good.
strike.name: Strike

sunderingChop.flavor:
Downward blow meant to split a shield.

The Vanguard's smiths measured their work by it. A shield that survived three chops was sent to the wall; one that did not was sent back to the forge with the smith's name chalked upon it.

Few names were chalked twice.
sunderingChop.name: Sundering Chop
sunderingChop.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Draw {draw} card.

sunderplate.flavor:
Joint-splitting blow of the Wardens.

Devised in the years of the Mark Trade with the Court's knights in mind, lest the Court forget which flame kept it fed. No occasion of its use is recorded.

Beside the drill, a knight's gorget, its crest scratched out.

supernova.flavor:
Brightest working in the charts.

The final predictive chart forecasts a light great enough to burn the paper it is drawn upon. The Starwatch took it for the fate of a star.

The chart is unsigned and undated. The apprentices swore it was not among the sheets they left upon his desk.

sweepingBlow.flavor:
Wide swing for the viaduct.

Where the corrupted come three abreast and the stone is narrow. The Forsaken councils teach that the viaducts were always built to funnel something, long before there were corrupted to funnel.

The corrupted walk them because the stone expects a crowd.
sweepingBlow.name: Sweeping Blow

technique.flavor:
Steps cut into the road.

Too even to be natural, too worn to be recent. The Forsaken credit them to the climbers before. They run past the farthest point any Forsaken is known to have reached, and some lead onto the viaducts, older than the kingdom.

Climbers before you cut steps. Use them.
technique.name: Footwork

thornHaloCard.flavor:
Crown of briar, worn at the feast of the Founding.

In memory of the first Saint, who by Chapel tradition wore thorns in the caldera; each thorn stood for a name carried. In the Long Winter, the Thorn Matriarch grew a crown of her own.

The remnant counts her a Saint. She was a Warden, and never swore to them.
thornHaloCard.name: Thorn Halo
thornHaloCard.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, apply 1 Crimson Blight to ALL enemies.

thornMatriarch.entwiningRoots.name: Entwining_Roots
thornMatriarch.entwiningRoots.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed to the enemy. Charges for 1 turn.

thousandCutsRogue.flavor:
Many small cuts, each undoing a stitch.

The surgeons called it the procedure run backward, and forbade it, for a courtier sewn to his post had sworn an oath. The winter after the Burning, a surgeon was found unstitching his own wife from the palace stair.

The surgeons' day-book records only a failed stitching.

timeDilation.flavor:
Slowing of the moment, after the eclipse.

By the Starwatch's reckoning the eclipse lasted a single night. By the Observatory clock, it has not ended. Anselm, keeper of the clock, refused to reset it.

He was found beside it, standing as he stood when the light went.
timeDilation.name: Time Dilation

toxicVolley.flavor:
Sedative vials, broken into the river fog.

Loosed upwind of the bridge watch, which slept through three robberies. The river smelled of it for weeks.

The watch ledger records those weeks as quiet, and commends the men for their vigilance.
toxicVolley.name: Toxic Volley
toxicVolley.textTemplate: Apply {venom} Venom and {weak} Weak to ALL enemies.

transfusion.flavor:
Communion of blood, between Saint and dying.

Blood poured from cup to cup, for the dying of good family. The rubric speaks of the Saint giving, never receiving. Novice Wen wrote that the flow ran both ways.

The Saints rose from the rite looking younger.
transfusion.name: Transfusion

transmute.flavor:
Cinder spent in the palm.

For a moment, the hand that holds it does not shake. The hamlets hold that each cinder was someone once, and forbid spending a cinder one took oneself.

Those who return from the ring have mostly broken that rule.
transmute.name: Transmute

twinFang.flavor:
Two knives, worn crosswise.

One for the hound, one for its handler. The weald's blight-hounds were the Wardens' before the Burning, and run yet with Bastion kennelmen who turned with the pack.

A handler may be reasoned with, briefly. Never twice.
twinFang.name: Twin Fang

twinPrick.flavor:
Two small wounds, set close together.

The Court's surgeons recorded them as bites when they found them upon bodies along the bridges. Their receipts give the hour, the bridge and the fee for the inquest. Not one case was closed.

The dock children call it the Surgeon's Signature.
twinPrick.name: Twin Prick
twinPrick.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Prepared: deal {damage.2} damage {hits.2} times. Consume Prepared.

twinbladeFlurry.flavor:
Two short blades, worked in turn, as the weald's sellswords used them.

Too poor for a shield and too proud to carry a Warden's, they were hired for the Bastion's narrow gates. It is said part of their wage was paid in marks rather than coin: a right to the city's warmth.

Those who refused the mark are the ones who tell of it.
twinbladeFlurry.name: Twinblade Flurry

twinkling.flavor:
Light drawn from a varying star.

The Astronomer recorded its variation nightly for many years, and drew no conclusion, as was his rule. In the last spring before the Burning, he spent three nights upon it alone.

The charts of those nights are not in the series.
twinkling.name: Twinkling

umbralWard.flavor:
Ward of shadow, after the eclipse.

During the eclipse the Observatory cast no shadow, which the Starwatch recorded as a curiosity of the light. The apprentices upon the terrace cast shadows as ever.

Theirs fell toward the Observatory, not away.
umbralWard.name: Umbral Ward
umbralWard.textTemplate: Prepare Spell Counter. Gain {block} Block. Starstone: {block.2} instead.

unbreakable.flavor:
Order to hold the Fell Courtyard gate.

Dated, signed and never countermanded. The gate log continues past the Burning in a second hand, one entry each night, at the same hour. The gate still stands; the wall on either side does not.

No relief is recorded.

unbreakable.textTemplate: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. (Block capped at 30.)

upgrade.textTemplate: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. (Block capped at 40.)

urgentHeal.flavor:
Rite of the Furnace Chapel, for wounds taken in its service.

Performed swiftly, its prayer cut to the first line. The rubric bids the wound be bound beneath the brand, never over it, that the mark be left clear.

We bind the wound beneath the unspent brand.
urgentHeal.name: Urgent Heal

valkyrieShade.bloodFeather.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed to the enemy.

vanish.flavor:
Art of the unmarked beneath the bridges.

Taught to the docks by those who lived under the Citadel's bridges before the Decree, when to be seen was to be entered on a roll. Under the bridges there is nothing but ice.

Most of those teachers vanished in the end. Where to, the docks cannot agree.

venomcoat.flavor:
Sedative paste of the Court's surgeons.

Sold by the vial to courtiers who could not sleep in the weeks before the Decree. The docks found it served a blade as well as a cup of wine.

The label promises a dreamless night.
venomcoat.name: Venomcoat

vesperWard.flavor:
Ward of the Chapel's evening bell-ringers.

A chime rung at vespers to close the day. Its bell was taken long ago; only the frame and the ward remain. Climbers who carry it say it rings at dusk regardless.

A Chapel ward, rung at vespers. The bell is gone.
vesperWard.name: Vesper Ward

viperStrike.flavor:
Short blade, long wait.

The docks coat the edge at dusk and let the cold carry the rest. A viper strikes once and withdraws, and the ice-cutters admire the manners of it. The bridge watch logs the wound as a scratch, the fee as a gift.

The wounded rarely admire anything by morning.
viperStrike.name: Viper Strike

wakingNightmare.flavor:
The dream does not end when the eyes open.

Apprentices who slept at the long lens woke describing rooms the Observatory never built. The Astronomer logged them as visions. The cleaning staff logged them as tenants.

Both logs agree the rooms were occupied.
wakingNightmare.name: Waking Nightmare
wakingNightmare.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {confused} Confused. May add {sleep} Sleep buildup.

warSurgeon.flavor:
Field practice of the Bastion's surgeon-wardens.

They stitched wounds upon the wall, never below it, for a Warden stitched standing remained a Warden, and one carried to the stool was struck from the roll. The Wardens claimed their surgeons outdid the Chapel's physicians.

The Chapel's own figures burned with the Chapel.

upgrade.textTemplate: Heal 2 HP for every 3 Bleed on all enemies. Exhaust.

warcry.flavor:
The bell-roll, shouted.

A custom of the gates farthest from the Bellfoundry, where the bell could not be heard. The Wardens held that the roll bore power of its own if read in order. Sellswords, who were not on it, shouted it all the same.

It is said the Bell Keeper answers, with a cracked bell.

wardingLunge.flavor:
Guarded advance into the breaking stance.

Taught as the moment to cease holding and begin taking ground. The Warden was to know that moment by the bell. When the Bellfoundry bell cracked, a new line was added beneath.

Know it by the smell of the courtyard.
wardingLunge.name: Warding Lunge

wardingStar.flavor:
Guarding light, after the Fixed Lamp.

A star above the coast that did not move with the others. The Starwatch took it for a flaw of the lens and reground the lens twice. The star remained.

After the Spire was finished, the log names it only "the error".
wardingStar.name: Warding Star
wardingStar.textTemplate: Prepare Spell Counter. Gain {block} Block. Starstone: draw {draw} card.

warmLitany.flavor:
First prayer of the Furnace Chapel's novices.

Said over a small hurt, to keep it warm. The novices were taught its words were older than the Chapel, found by the first Saint cut into the caldera wall.

We give the name. We keep the warmth.
warmLitany.name: Warm Litany

warriorsVow.flavor:
Contract of the sellswords of the Fell Courtyard.

Hold the gate until relieved; pay in advance. The weald's hired blades held a paid contract sacred, having few other sacred things, and the Wardens despised them for it.

The last was signed the week before the Burning. Its date of release is blank.
warriorsVow.name: Warrior's Vow
warriorsVow.textTemplate: Innate. Enter a Stance of your choice. Exhaust.

waxingMoonCard.flavor:
Sorcery of the Starwatch, drawn from the moon-table.

In the last years before the Burning, the Astronomer observed that as the moon waxed, the coal in the Crown dimmed in equal measure. He named it coincidence, and kept the moon-table no longer.

What he would not record, his apprentices remembered.
waxingMoonCard.name: Waxing Moon
waxingMoonCard.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, apply 2 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.

whirlingGuard.flavor:
A spin that is both parry and cut.

Dock dancers performed it for the Court at feast days, with painted wooden knives. After the Burning they were seen performing it on the quay, with other knives, and without the paint.

No feast has been held since.
whirlingGuard.name: Whirling Guard
whirlingGuard.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Deal {damage} damage {hits} times to ALL enemies.

witheringTouch.flavor:
Touch that withers growth.

Permitted by the rubric upon the weeds of the weald's field-shrines, and nothing else. In the years the Field Flame dimmed, a clause was added forbidding its use upon crops.

The clause is dated after three harvests had failed, and signed by a Saint absent from the roll of Saints.
witheringTouch.name: Withering Touch

wound.flavor:
A cut that closed wrong.

It knits into a hard ridge that aches before the weather turns. Climbers call it the road keeping its share.

The hamlets' older word for it means owed.
wound.name: Wound

zealotryCard.flavor:
Creed of the Feral Ember.

Each wound is a door the fire walks through. Its priests bless wounds rather than bind them, and hold that the Chapel knew as much, and hid it behind a ledger.

Its converts do not live long. More come each week.
zealotryCard.name: Zealotry
zealotryCard.textTemplate: Whenever you lose HP, deal 3 damage to a random enemy.
